classification.difficultyReason: Model dilution by conserving the mass of salt while increasing the solution volume, then solve a linear equation.

content.prompt: A chemist has 500 mL of a salt solution that contains 2% salt, in units of $\mathrm{g/cm^3}$. How much water must be added to reduce the concentration to 0.5%?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ mL be the volume of water added. Since $1\text{ mL}=1\text{ cm}^3$, the original mass of salt is $0.02\times500=10\text{ g}$. Adding water leaves this mass unchanged, and the new volume is $(500+x)$ mL.
$$\begin{align*}0.005(500+x)&=10\\2.5+0.005x&=10\\0.005x&=7.5\\x&=1500\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $1500\text{ mL}=1.5\text{ L}$ of water must be added.
